title: Kepler to Müller, 17/27 October 1629
author: Johannes Kepler
summary: Amid the ruin of the war, Kepler sends two journeymen to Leipzig to buy a press, have type cast and paper made for printing Tycho Brahe's observations, and asks Müller to advance money from his and Bartsch's funds; with a note on the Danish astronomy of Longomontanus.

notes.note: Compositor (*collector*): the workman who sets the type, letter by letter, into pages.
Pressman (*impressor*): the workman who inks the set type and pulls the sheets on the press.
See the [map of the cities mentioned in this correspondence](https://drive.vjbe.net/2026-10-31-kepler.webp).

Thalers, named after the silver coins of Joachimsthal in Bohemia. A thaler was roughly four days’ wages for a Leipzig carpenter. Allen’s Leipzig series, taken from M. J. Elsas, *Umriss einer Geschichte der Preise und Löhne in Deutschland*, vol. 2 (1940), gives prices and wages in pfennig (Denar). At 24 groschen of 12 pfennig, a Reichsthaler was 288 pfennig, against a carpenter’s summer wage of 72 pfennig a day in 1630. (See “Leipzig 1564–1914 (Allen)” in the [Global Price and Income History Group’s data files](https://gpih.ucdavis.edu/Datafilelist.htm#Europe).)
Kepler sends a compositor and a pressman to buy type, which must be cast by a typefounder (*fusor*).

Printer (*typographus*): the master of a printing house, who employed compositors and pressmen. Celebrated master printers included Aldus Manutius, Robert Estienne, Oporinus and Plantin (Eisenstein, 1980, p. 691).
“The Danish Astronomy” is a book: the *Astronomia Danica* (1622) by Christen Sørensen Longomontanus, Tycho Brahe’s longest-serving assistant at Hven, later professor at Copenhagen.
Wallenstein, Duke of Friedland and Sagan, who paid for Kepler's press.

references: Eisenstein, Elizabeth L. *The Printing Press as an Agent of Change: Communications and Cultural Transformations in Early Modern Europe*. Vol. 2. 1980.
